name: Transparency
definition: Be open about as many things as possible. By making information public, we reduce the threshold to contribution and make collaboration easier. Transparency is not communication: something existing in the handbook does not mean it should not also be communicated to the people who need to understand it.

rows.situation: When a decision is made in a call
rows.under: Leaves it in people's heads, and the reasoning is gone in a month.
rows.justRight: Writes it in the handbook where anyone can find it, including people not yet hired.
rows.over: Publishes so much unedited detail that the signal is impossible to find.

rows.under: Quietly updates the plan, and people work from the old one.
rows.justRight: Says what changed and why, in the place people already look.
rows.over: Narrates every reconsideration in public until nobody can tell what is decided.

rows.under: Fixes it quietly and hopes nobody noticed.
rows.justRight: Says you made a mistake, in public, and says what you learned.
rows.over: Confesses so routinely that people cannot tell which mistakes mattered.

rows.situation: When the news is bad and not yet final
rows.under: Waits for certainty, and people plan against a picture you know is wrong.
rows.justRight: Shares what you know and what is still open, and marks clearly which is which.
rows.over: Broadcasts every unconfirmed worry, and the team runs on alarm.

rows.situation: When the information is genuinely restricted
rows.under: Shares it anyway, because openness is the default.
rows.justRight: Keeps what must be private private, and is transparent about the fact that a boundary exists.
rows.over: Classifies so much as sensitive that the default quietly inverts to closed.

rows.situation: When it is already in the handbook
rows.under: Sends the link and treats the matter as communicated.
rows.justRight: Tells the people who need to act, directly. Transparency is not communication.
rows.over: Repeats the same announcement in every channel until people filter you out.
